question: Does an unfreeze-then-angular-velocity-write activation route deliver both declared signed initial hinge rates into native Godot/Jolt and activate opposing motor impulse plus absorbed motor work in each motor-enabled braking cell while paired motor-disabled cells retain exact zero motor telemetry?
scope: One native zero-gravity world, one build, four isolated one-hinge cells, one exact solver step, and four retained samples. This is a mechanism-activation characterization only.

native_control_flow: JoltBody3D::set_angular_velocity stores a static or kinematic body's value in angular_surface_velocity rather than rigid-body motion state
JoltBody3D::set_mode clears angular_surface_velocity after changing the body from static to rigid
source_diagnosis.source_supported_explanation: R24D10's scene property retained the declared rate, but the write occurred while each child was frozen/static. The later unfreeze changed the native mode and cleared the native angular_surface_velocity before the first solver step. This explains why the first retained post-step rate and braking telemetry were zero without changing the immutable R24D10 result.

ordered_operations: disable PhysicsServer3D before constructing the viewport world
construct all four cells and attach the viewport to SceneTree
write child.angular_velocity from the declared canonical signed rate
read back the scene property and PhysicsServer3D BODY_STATE_ANGULAR_VELOCITY before enabling physics
enable PhysicsServer3D at one physics-frame boundary
read exact native step token one at the next boundary
disable PhysicsServer3D before token two can begin

runtime_freeze.engine_build_reuse_scope: Exact unchanged native runtime bytes only. No R24D10 campaign result, evaluation, source qualification, or physical conclusion is reused as R24D12 evidence.

mechanism_witness_rule.motor_enabled_cell_rule: The exact pre-step scene and PhysicsServer canonical rate readbacks equal the declared nonzero real_t projection; the retained current native sample has nonzero signed_motor_impulse_nms opposing that signed pre-rate, absorbed_motor_work_j greater than zero, and net_motor_work_j less than zero.
mechanism_witness_rule.motor_disabled_cell_rule: The exact pre-step scene and PhysicsServer canonical rate readbacks equal the paired declared nonzero real_t projection; signed_motor_impulse_nms, positive_motor_work_j, absorbed_motor_work_j, and net_motor_work_j are exactly zero.
mechanism_witness_rule.positive_outcome: Both signed motor-enabled cells and both paired disabled controls satisfy their mechanism rules.
mechanism_witness_rule.negative_outcome: The exact finite execution is otherwise valid but one or more mechanism rules lack a witness.
mechanism_witness_rule.implementation_invalid_outcome: The declared source, runtime, fixture, activation, exact-step, identity, refusal, or report-shape contract is violated.

adequacy.threshold_provenance: No empirical threshold is selected. Strict nonzero direction and work signs follow from the previously declared absorbed-work mechanism itself; exact zeros define the paired disabled negative controls.
adequacy.cohort_argument: This is the complete declared four-cell fixture rather than a sample from a morphology or performance population. One exact solver step is adequate to determine whether initial state reaches the solver and whether the braking mechanism activates in each signed direction; it is not adequate for accuracy, repeatability, robustness, recovery, or locomotion claims.
adequacy.why_no_shortened_physics_ghost: The complete physical question is already one world, four cells, one solver step, and four samples. A second physics ghost would duplicate the finite mechanism question instead of only proving code reachability.
